rules.label: Confidence
rules.text: Confidence in the extracted claim, not overall source trust.

rules.label: Corroboration Status
rules.text: Whether additional independent linguistic evidence is still required.

rules.label: Human Validation
rules.text: Separate from AI/source review. Native speaker/expert approval happens here.

rules.label: Production Status
rules.text: Candidate = usable for research; Hold = unresolved; Approved = eligible for learner-facing generation; Rejected = do not use.

rules.label: Audio rule
rules.text: Do not infer correct pronunciation from spelling alone. Tone/pronunciation fields remain unresolved until audio or expert evidence supports them.

rules.label: Generation rule
rules.text: AI may generate exercises from Approved knowledge; it should not invent new language facts while generating an exercise.

rules.label: Publication rule
rules.text: Candidate knowledge is not learner-facing truth. Context-sensitive, dialect-sensitive, culturally editorial, or weakly corroborated items remain Hold until human/expert validation.

rules.label: Current pass
rules.text: 30 knowledge objects drafted primarily from Harvard ELIAS plus source-provenance information from the Welmers/ERIC record.

rules.label: Trust Level
rules.text: Overall shorthand only. Retrieval should rank authority for the specific claim type, not blindly use overall trust.

rules.label: Corroboration Required
rules.text: No = may establish suitable facts independently; Preferred = seek another source; Yes = cannot establish knowledge independently; Not for linguistic facts = technical dataset/tool only.

rules.label: Rights principle
rules.text: Free access does not equal permission to store, adapt, train on, or commercially reuse. Treat websites, APIs, datasets, books and audio as separate rights objects.

rules.label: Dialect principle
rules.text: Never silently normalize dialect-specific material into 'Igbo'. Preserve dialect provenance and label Standard/Central Igbo explicitly.

rules.label: Validation principle
rules.text: AI reviewed means the registry entry has been researched, not that underlying language content is production-approved.

rules.label: Required Knowledge IDs
rules.text: Links the capability to grounded Knowledge Registry objects. This is the core bridge between language truth and curriculum.

rules.label: Status
rules.text: Draft = defined but not ready; Knowledge Gap = missing/weak underlying knowledge; Ready for Lesson = knowledge approved enough to design exercises; Validated = capability itself tested/approved.

rules.label: MVP Rule
rules.source: capability registry v0.1 → MVP Lesson Map
rules.text: Every learner-facing Igbo form used in the lesson must trace to an Approved Knowledge Object.

rules.label: Current Blocker
rules.source: capability registry v0.1 → MVP Lesson Map
rules.text: The required knowledge objects are still Candidate/Hold and need cross-source corroboration plus native-speaker/audio validation.

rules.label: Core principle
rules.text: Exercises are reusable teaching/assessment mechanics, not a fixed lesson sequence. Runtime selects the smallest useful intervention based on learner evidence.

rules.label: Content rule
rules.text: Approved knowledge can be used authoritatively. Candidate enrichment may be referenced in design but is not treated as authoritative teaching content until validated.

Natural follow-on after greeting in Harvard dialogue.

knowledge.Communicative Function: Time-specific greeting used in early morning hours
knowledge.Register / Context: Conversational; informal to semi-formal; all relationships
knowledge.Grammar / Structure Note: Construction: [Time period] + [ọma] (good). Follows standard Igbo time-noun + adjective pattern.
knowledge.Cultural / Usage Note: Used early in day; carries warmth. Alternative to generic Kedu? when time-awareness is appropriate. Common in daily greeting.
knowledge.Tone / Pronunciation Note: [ụ́tụ́tụ ọ́ma] — High tone on first two syllables of ụtụtụ; high tone on ọ. Should sound warm, not clipped.

knowledge.Human Validation: Needs validation - pronunciation and register appropriateness

knowledge.English / Explanation: May it be well / Until we see again (natural Igbo goodbye)
knowledge.Communicative Function: Primary Igbo closing expression; conveys well-wishing and expectation of future connection
knowledge.Register / Context: Friendly, warm; appropriate across all relationships
knowledge.Grammar / Structure Note: Construction: Ka (may/let) + ọ (it/one) + dị (be/remain). Subjunctive mood.
knowledge.Cultural / Usage Note: Authentic Igbo goodbye; avoids English translation 'goodbye'. Signals continuing relationship and well-wishing.
knowledge.Source Evidence Summary: Consistently taught across multiple established curricula as primary goodbye.

capabilities.Learning Objective: Recognize, initiate, and respond to a basic Igbo greeting exchange.
capabilities.Learner Outcome: Can participate in a short reciprocal greeting without being shown the target response.
capabilities.Enrichment Knowledge IDs: KNW-029 (Ụtụtụ ọma), KNW-030 (Mgbede ọma), KNW-031 (Nne), KNW-032 (Nna), KNW-033 (Nwanna), KNW-034 (Ọ dị mma ịhụta gị)
capabilities.Cultural / Pragmatic Knowledge: Hierarchical respect protocols (younger greets first, different handshake by gender), age-based greeting modifications, status-based greeting variations, physical expression protocols
capabilities.Recognition Criteria: Understands the intent of a basic greeting when heard or read.
capabilities.Production Criteria: Can independently produce an appropriate response and initiate the greeting.
capabilities.Interaction Criteria: Can sustain a short reciprocal greeting exchange for 2–3 turns.
capabilities.Knowledge Gaps / Research Needs: Corroborate Kedụ?, Ọ dị mma, Kedụ maka gị?; validate tone/pronunciation and contemporary naturalness.

capabilities.Learning Objective: Ask someone's name and introduce yourself during a basic social interaction.
capabilities.Learner Outcome: Can exchange names naturally after greeting someone.
capabilities.Enrichment Knowledge IDs: KNW-035 (Chioma), KNW-036 (Ifeoma), KNW-037 (Chinedu), KNW-038 (Ifeanyi), KNW-039 (Aha ọ dị mma)
capabilities.Cultural / Pragmatic Knowledge: Theophoric naming patterns, name meanings as cultural values, connection between name and parental hope/circumstances
capabilities.Recognition Criteria: Understands a name question and recognizes a self-introduction.
capabilities.Production Criteria: Can ask another person's name and state their own name without a complete phrase prompt.
capabilities.Interaction Criteria: Can complete the name-exchange portion of a first-meeting conversation.
capabilities.Knowledge Gaps / Research Needs: Corroborate Aha m bụ… and Kedụ aha gị?; validate tone and whether additional natural variants are needed.
capabilities.Notes: Grammar can remain implicit in MVP unless testing shows explanation is necessary.

capabilities.Learning Objective: Recognize and use a basic parting expression to end a social interaction naturally.
capabilities.Learner Outcome: Can recognize that an interaction is ending and respond with or initiate an appropriate basic goodbye.
capabilities.Enrichment Knowledge IDs: KNW-040 (Ka ọ dị), KNW-041 (Ọ dị mma ịgbakọ na gị), KNW-042 (A ga enyụ ọnụ)
capabilities.Cultural / Pragmatic Knowledge: Time-of-day considerations for closing, status/age-based closing variations, expectation of future connection as cultural value
capabilities.Recognition Criteria: Recognizes Ka emesia as a parting expression in context.
capabilities.Production Criteria: Can independently use the parting expression when leaving.
capabilities.Interaction Criteria: Can close the MVP first-meeting conversation without being shown the answer.
capabilities.Knowledge Gaps / Research Needs: Corroborate Ka emesia; determine whether one additional common parting form is needed for a robust capability.
capabilities.Notes: May be thin with one phrase; lesson-level interaction gives it context.

lesson.Lesson Outcome: By the end of this lesson, the learner can have a simple first encounter in Igbo: greet someone, exchange names, and close the interaction.
lesson.Capabilities: CAP-001 Basic Greeting Exchange; CAP-002 Exchange Names; CAP-003 Close an Interaction
lesson.Final Assessment Concept: Learner meets an AI character with minimal scaffolding and completes a short interaction: greeting → reciprocal response → name exchange → parting.
lesson.MVP Rule: Every learner-facing Igbo form used in the lesson must trace to an Approved Knowledge Object.
lesson.Current Blocker: The required knowledge objects are still Candidate/Hold and need cross-source corroboration plus native-speaker/audio validation.
lesson.Not in MVP Lesson: Origin, residence, plural/group greetings, welcomes, time-of-day/regional greetings, and respectful greeting scenarios are intentionally deferred.

routing.What It Means: Learner can already perform most/all of the capability.
routing.Typical Evidence Pattern: Strong comprehension + independent production; some dimensions may still be unknown.
routing.Router Goal: Verify missing dimensions with minimal friction, then advance.
routing.Important Rule: Never reteach what the learner can demonstrate.
routing.Learner Model Note: KNOW is a routing summary, not a stored mastery label.

routing.What It Means: Learner has meaningful prior exposure but a specific gap.
routing.Typical Evidence Pattern: Examples: understands but answers in English; can respond but cannot initiate; intelligible wording but pronunciation weak.
routing.Router Goal: Identify the precise gap and retrieve the smallest targeted intervention.
routing.Important Rule: Do not restart the capability from the beginning.
routing.Learner Model Note: Track dimensions separately: comprehension, recall, initiation, pronunciation, etc.

routing.What It Means: Learner shows little/no understanding of the capability.
routing.Router Goal: Provide contextual observation + light instruction, then return to communication quickly.
routing.Example Path: ENC → OBS → REC → DISC/IMI → RCL → PROD → INT
routing.Important Rule: More support is allowed, but still avoid unnecessary exercises.
routing.Learner Model Note: State should update continuously as evidence arrives.

evidence.Demonstrated When: Learner appropriately interprets an encountered spoken greeting.

evidence.Demonstrated When: Learner independently asks another person's name.

evidence.Demonstrated When: Learner completes the name-exchange portion of a first-meeting conversation.
evidence.Notes: Enrichment reactions to names are not required.

evidence.Notes: Contextual recognition matters, not only translation.

evidence.Demonstrated When: Learner uses the closing in an appropriate social situation.
evidence.Notes: Pragmatic variation can expand later as knowledge is validated.

runtimeRules.Meaning: The learner should experience a social need before the product exposes teaching mechanics whenever practical.
Use learner evidence to target the actual gap; do not restart from meaning if comprehension is already demonstrated.
Allow time and optional help; expand from light cue → stronger cue/model → micro-practice only as needed.
Every intervention must restore the learner to the original social opportunity so new knowledge is immediately used.
Unknown material does not always require OBS → infer → explain → imitate. Context may make a lighter intervention sufficient.
The Router must consider both learner need and how much remediation the current encounter can absorb without becoming unpleasant.
If further remediation would damage pacing, let the narrative progress and gather missing CAP evidence later.
Language may appear for richness/culture/context without being assessed, explained, or added to mastery requirements.
Successful communication is often confirmed by natural NPC continuation rather than explicit 'correct' UI.
Use correction/explanation when misunderstanding would compound, the learner requests it, or communication cannot continue.
If speech/evidence is ambiguous, gather another attempt or provide graceful support rather than penalizing.
Repeated struggle should eventually trigger enough support to complete the social moment and move on.

patterns.Primary Job: Confirm successful communication without interrupting it.
patterns.Typical Trigger: Response is communicatively successful with sufficient confidence.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: NPC naturally reacts/continues; no explicit correctness screen.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Positive evidence already captured by Evaluator.
patterns.Return Behavior: No detour; next beat or natural continuation.
patterns.AI / Deterministic: Mostly deterministic expression of Router decision.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Do not add praise/checkmarks after every successful turn.

patterns.Primary Job: Let learner hear the same input again.
patterns.Typical Trigger: Learner requests replay or listening evidence is uncertain.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: Same audio repeats; conversation visually remains in place.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Replay itself is assistance metadata; later response is evaluated with that support known.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Do not interpret replay request as failure.

patterns.Primary Job: Reduce perceptual difficulty without revealing the answer.
patterns.Typical Trigger: Learner requests it or repeated listening suggests parsing difficulty.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Counts as listening support; may weaken independence evidence.
patterns.AI / Deterministic: Selection may be Router-driven; asset is pre-approved.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Do not synthesize arbitrary pronunciation variants at runtime.

patterns.Primary Job: Nudge meaning/action without supplying target language.
patterns.Typical Trigger: Learner appears close but needs situational cue.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: Short visual/social cue or non-answer prompt.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Light assistance; can still yield meaningful evidence depending on dimension.
patterns.AI / Deterministic: Router selects from authored hint types.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Hint must not accidentally contain the answer.

patterns.Primary Job: Support retrieval while preserving some learner production.
patterns.Typical Trigger: Recall/production gap after lighter help is insufficient.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: Beginning/structure of approved phrase, leaving learner to complete it.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Supported production; recall independence not demonstrated.
patterns.Return Behavior: Retry same social turn, then later seek S0 evidence.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Do not count completion as independent recall.

patterns.Primary Job: Give the learner the exact approved language they need.
patterns.Typical Trigger: Learner does not know target form or repeated attempts fail.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: ●/NPC plays or displays approved target response; replay available.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Teaching evidence / supported production, not independent recall.
patterns.Return Behavior: Recreate original social prompt and ask learner to use it.

patterns.Primary Job: Teach communicative function through a tiny example interaction.
patterns.Typical Trigger: Learner lacks comprehension/function knowledge and context alone is insufficient.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: Brief exchange between speakers or NPC demonstration; optional inference prompt.
patterns.Return Behavior: Return to original encounter after observation.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Keep brief; do not automatically turn into a quiz.

patterns.Typical Trigger: Learner needs more than a cue/model to proceed.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: 1–3 tightly scoped practice attempts using approved exercise inventory.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Produces supported/independent evidence according to scaffold.
patterns.Return Behavior: Must end by returning to the triggering conversation beat.
patterns.AI / Deterministic: Router selects exercises; bounded by choreography.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Never become an open-ended remediation loop.

patterns.Primary Job: Convert teaching into immediate communicative use.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: Original NPC/social prompt is naturally recreated.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Fresh evidence, with current scaffold level tracked.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Do not jump to a new exercise before the learner uses the new knowledge.

patterns.Primary Job: Preserve communication when meaning succeeds but form is imperfect.
patterns.Typical Trigger: Learner is understandable/appropriate but uses imperfect or non-target form.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: NPC responds to meaning and naturally models stronger approved form.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Positive functional evidence; form-specific gap may remain.
patterns.Return Behavior: Conversation continues; recast can be reinforced later.
patterns.AI / Deterministic: Evaluator identifies communicative success + form gap; runtime uses approved recast.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Do not silently validate materially wrong meaning; recast only when communication truly succeeded.

patterns.Typical Trigger: Meaning is wrong, response is socially inappropriate, or learner asks why.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: Brief direct correction/explanation, then target form.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Negative/inconclusive evidence already captured; subsequent attempts tracked separately.
patterns.Return Behavior: Return to same or safely reconstructed moment.
patterns.AI / Deterministic: Router-triggered; explanation constrained to approved knowledge.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Use when necessary, not as default feedback.

patterns.Primary Job: Resolve meaning when inference is insufficient or learner requests it.
patterns.Typical Trigger: Comprehension gap persists or explicit help requested.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Strong semantic assistance; does not demonstrate independent comprehension.
patterns.Return Behavior: Return to original prompt for supported then later independent use.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Translation is a tool, not a failure state.

patterns.Primary Job: Protect pacing and learner dignity after repeated struggle.
patterns.Typical Trigger: Experience budget is exhausted or repeated attempts are not productive.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: System supplies enough language/support to complete the social moment and moves on.
patterns.Evidence Effect: CAP may remain EMERGING/UNKNOWN; no fake mastery.
patterns.Return Behavior: Narrative continues/ends naturally; gap persists in learner model.

patterns.Primary Job: Give learner agency over support depth.
patterns.Learner Sees/Experiences: Compact help affordance expands to relevant options: replay, hint, meaning, model.
patterns.Evidence Effect: Assistance type is recorded; request itself is not negative evidence.
patterns.Key Guardrail: Help should be available without making the UI feel permanently instructional.

helpLadder.What changes: Nothing is revealed; learner acts in context.
Makes the situation/input easier to perceive without giving target response.
helpLadder.Use when: Learner may understand/know it but needs a nudge.
Meaning seems known; retrieval/production is the gap.

helpLadder.What changes: Briefly isolates one gap for practice.

helpLadder.Evidence / scaffold implication: Fresh attempt; strongest evidence when support has been removed.

helpLadder.What changes: Supplies enough support to finish and defers remaining mastery.
helpLadder.Use when: Further remediation would harm pacing or confidence.
helpLadder.Evidence / scaffold implication: Capability remains incomplete; lesson can continue/end.

mvpBoundaries.Defer / Research Later: Final Igbo TTS/voice vendor/model choice and tone-quality validation
Tone-aware pronunciation grading until technically credible

humanReviewQueue.Review Question: Would you naturally say Kedụ? in this situation, and how would you pronounce it?
How do you use Ndewo/Ndeewo today? Which spelling/pronunciation feels natural, and where?
When would you use Daalụ as 'hello' versus 'thank you'?
Would you teach Ụtụtụ ọma as a beginner 'good morning'? What would you personally say?
humanReviewQueue.Why Human Review Matters: Potential mismatch between teaching form and lived usage

humanReviewQueue.Review Question: How accurate is the age/gender greeting etiquette today, including diaspora contexts?
Which regional morning greetings are actually current/common today?
How should we explain -nụ to beginners without overgeneralizing?
What audio/tone representation should the product store for beginner phrases?

fields.Lesson Outcome: By the end of this lesson, the learner can have a simple first encounter in Igbo: greet someone, exchange names, and close the interaction.
fields.Capabilities: CAP-001 Basic Greeting Exchange; CAP-002 Exchange Names; CAP-003 Close an Interaction

fields.Success Continuation: NPC reacts as if understood and conversation remains open.
fields.Allowed Intervention Families: Replay; slower audio; hint; model; observe; focused practice.

knownDefects.what: Two ID schemes in one sheet, with a numeric collision.
knownDefects.evidence: Rows 2–31 use IGB-KNW-001…030 with Domain ID DOMAIN-001. Rows 32–45 use KNW-029…042 with Domain ID "Greetings & Initial Social Interaction". IGB-KNW-029 (a source/standardization rule) and KNW-029 (the phrase Ụtụtụ ọma) are different rows sharing a suffix.

knownDefects.what: The same phrase appears twice with contradictory status.
knownDefects.evidence: IGB-KNW-012: Ụtụtụ ọma — Confidence Medium, Production Status Hold; KNW-029: Ụtụtụ ọma — Confidence High, Production Status Approved

knownDefects.what: Nine rows are shifted one column left from Tone / Pronunciation Note onward, so those cells cannot be read literally.
knownDefects.evidence: IGB-KNW-022 reads Tone / Pronunciation Note = "IGB-SRC-001" and Confidence = "Must be human/community validated; culturally variable".

knownDefects.what: IGB-KNW-016 and IGB-KNW-017 are swapped in three exercise rows.
knownDefects.evidence: CAP002-REC ("Hear the name question and identify what the speaker wants to know") cites IGB-KNW-016, which is "Aha m bụ …" — the answer, not the question.
